title: How to Make a Frothy Hazelnut Latte Using a Handheld Frother
meta_description: Learn how to make a cafe-quality hazelnut latte with a handheld frother. Follow our easy guide for perfect foam and rich nutty flavor at home.
html:
There is something incredibly satisfying about that first sip of a creamy, nutty latte. While visiting your favorite local coffee shop is great, you can actually replicate that experience in your own kitchen without spending $6 per cup. The secret to that professional texture isn't an expensive espresso machine—it's a simple, powerful tool. Making a hazelnut latte with handheld frother technology is the fastest way to get a cloud of foam and a rich flavor profile right before you head out the door.

Gather Your Ingredients and Gear

Before you start, gather everything you need. To get the best results, I recommend using a glass or a wide-mouthed jar for frothing; this gives the milk room to expand and prevents messy overflows. You'll need:

  • 1 shot of espresso or 1/2 cup of strong brewed coffee
  • 1 cup of milk (whole milk foams best, but oat milk is a fantastic dairy-free alternative)
  • 1-2 tablespoons of hazelnut syrup (depending on your sweetness preference)
  • The Milk Frother for that essential cafe-style foam

Brewing the Base for Your Hazelnut Latte

Start by preparing your coffee base. If you have an espresso machine or an Aeropress, pull a concentrated shot. If not, brew a small amount of very strong coffee using a French press or standard drip machine. While the coffee is still piping hot, stir in your hazelnut syrup. Mixing the syrup into the coffee rather than the milk ensures the flavor is evenly distributed and won't settle at the bottom of the mug.

Pour the sweetened coffee into your favorite large mug. This leaves plenty of room at the top for the frothy layer we are about to create.

How to Get the Perfect Foam with a Handheld Frother

This is where the magic happens. To make a high-quality hazelnut latte with handheld frother techniques, temperature is key. If you're using dairy, heat your milk to about 150°F. You can do this in a small saucepan on the stove or in the microwave for about 45-60 seconds. Avoid boiling the milk, as scorched milk won't hold bubbles as well and can taste burnt.

Pour the warm milk into your frothing vessel. Insert the Milk Frother at a slight angle just below the surface of the liquid. Turn it on and let it create a vortex. As the milk begins to foam and rise, slowly lower the frother deeper into the cup to incorporate the bubbles into the body of the milk. This creates a "micro-foam" texture that is silky rather than just bubbly.

Assembling Your Cafe-Style Drink

Once your milk has doubled in volume and looks thick and glossy, it's time to combine. Slowly pour the frothed milk over your hazelnut coffee. To keep the foam on top, hold back a bit of the liquid with a spoon and let the thickest foam slide gently into the center of the mug.

For an extra touch of luxury, you can sprinkle a pinch of cinnamon or a drop of hazelnut extract on top of the foam. The contrast between the bitter coffee, the sweet hazelnut, and the airy milk creates a balanced drink that rivals any professional barista's work.

Tips for Better Frothing Results

If you find your foam is collapsing too quickly, check your milk choice. Whole milk contains the fats and proteins necessary to stabilize air bubbles. If you prefer plant-based options, look for "Barista Edition" oat or almond milks, which are specifically engineered to froth better.

Another pro tip: always ensure your Milk Frother is clean and dry before use. Any residue from previous drinks can interfere with the surface tension of the milk, leading to larger, unstable bubbles rather than that creamy, velvet texture we're aiming for.

FAQ

Can I make a cold hazelnut latte with a handheld frother?

Yes! You can froth cold milk using the same method. While cold foam is slightly denser and doesn't expand as much as steamed milk, it creates a delicious, refreshing layer on top of iced coffee and hazelnut syrup.

Which milk froths the best for lattes?

Whole milk is the gold standard for stability and creaminess. However, oat milk is the best non-dairy alternative because its protein structure mimics dairy, allowing it to hold a peak for much longer than almond or soy milk.

How do I clean my handheld frother?

Cleaning is simple. Immediately after use, run the frother in a glass of warm, soapy water for a few seconds, then rinse it under clean running water. This prevents milk proteins from drying and sticking to the whisk.
